newsitem.title: CHINA: China to open new air route to Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: China to open new air route to Amsterdam.

text.p: China Southern Airlines will next month open a new air route linking Guangzhou city in southern Guangdong province with the Dutch capital Amsterdam, the China Youth Daily said on Friday.
The airline would operate flights using Boeing 777s or 767s from Guangzhou every Tuesday and Friday from November 26, the newspaper said.
The flights would include a stop-over in Beijing, with flying time on the 9,800-km (6,000-mile) route totalling almost 14 hours, it said.
The route would be China Southern Airlines' first to Europe, it said.
The UK October PMI, rising for the fifth consecutive month, hit an 18-month high at 54.5 percent, well above analysts' forecasts of 53.0 percent.
"Having seen an interest rate rise this week and comments that we might have another in the future... those (PMI) numbers took all of the (upward) momentum out of the sytem," said one dealer.
The FTSE 100 firmed at the open and and climbed as high as 3,988.0, buoyed by a stronger gilt market and a good performance on Wall Street overnight ahead of today's economic data.
The U.S. employment numbers are important because they will provide some of the best clues as to how the world's biggest economy is faring.

Economics surveyed by Reuters were expecting U.S. payrolls to show a rise of 212,000 in October, after the unexpected 40,000 decline in September. The October unemployment rate was seen unchanged from September at 5.2 percent.
"Everyone is just very cautious ahead of these numbers," another added.

If the U.S. report reveals continued weaknesses in the U.S. labour market, UK shares will rally with Wall Street. However, the dealer said, "I don't think will see the market run away with the (U.S.) elections next week, the FOMC meeting on November 13 and the UK budget out on November 26."
Other data due out of the U.S. this afternoon include September leading indicators, the October National Assocation of Purchasing Managers index, and September factory orders.
Among individual stocks, shares in BSkyB rebounded after an initial decline amid rumours that News Corp is abandoning plans of issuing convertible preferred securities, market makers said.
BSkyB declined to comment. A week ago, NewsCorp said it intended to sell $1 billion of preferred securities for the purchase of stock in its 40-percent-owned BSkyB.
Shares in BSkyB were up 4p to 582-1/2p, after initially falling to 567-3/4 after the company reported disappointing subscriber growth in its first quarter.

Elsewhere, shares in Yorkshire TV rose 12-1/2 pence to 1,280p as hopes resurfaced that Granada, which owns over 24 percent of Yorkshire, might launch a takeover bid. Granada said in September it had an open mind about a full bid for Yorkshire.
